source_state: Frozen working-tree 0.6 ownership slice after intrinsic-authority correction, before SDK9 packaging; not a final commit or Web acceptance claim

contract.ordinary_values: Constructors and composeStyle return deeply frozen detached values. Parents reuse privately proven immutable subtrees; caller-authored mutable inputs are copied and never frozen in place.
contract.registry: Per-VM package closure, weak table keys, numeric work/height metadata with no reference to the key or descendants
contract.shared_dag_accounting: Every reused occurrence charges its complete expanded work and relative height. Identity sharing cannot bypass either original copy limit.
contract.finalization: Private mutable assembly completes kind/style/drag/surface/children edits first. Generated output fields enter cached statistics without retroactively reducing the borrowed-input copy boundary.
contract.managed_exception: Exact registered virtualList/virtualGrid handles remain mutable engine-owned objects. Frozen ancestors containing them receive no pure immutable grant; later composition revisits those branches.
contract.authority: Package and scroll chunks capture all used sealed standard libraries and validation builtins before Game code executes. Scroll ownership uses captured rawget plus rawequal, not author-controlled equality.

actual_authority_reproduction.scope: Cache-only tiny projects embed the actual package and scroll source, then execute through the existing SDK8 native CLI. No Game source or player renderer is modified.
attacks_covered: Writable getfenv proxy shadows table.freeze/clone, math/string and validation builtins
setfenv replaces a public constructor function environment
Shadowed assert/pairs/type cannot grant mutable data or waive cycles, expanded work, cached work or cached depth
Matching __eq metatables and shadowed rawget/rawequal cannot impersonate a registered virtual node
actual_authority_reproduction.test_cleanup: Test captures its own trusted assertions/libraries and restores all changed environment keys and the public function environment even when the attack assertion fails

executed_focused_tests.command: cargo test -p unone-engine --test ui_immutable --test ui_components --test ui_slider_control -- --nocapture
coverage: Borrowed mutable input detachment, recursively frozen outputs and reuse across kits
Copy-on-write frozen style/padding and frozen child-array surface insertion, including a privately granted surface record
Slider drag metadata assembled before finalization and ordinary scroll snapshot detachment
Exact work/depth boundaries, repeated immutable DAG expansion, caller-frozen impostors, cloned values and cyclic/nonportable inputs
Managed materialization, failed-publication rollback, retirement and stale mutable descendants cannot hide in a pure grant
Reload publishes new values without modifying retained older Rust snapshots
Private weak registry does not retain obsolete nodes, rects or child arrays while the kit remains live
executed_focused_tests.weak_reclamation_method: A standalone unit VM keeps the kit and registry alive, stores obsolete values only through weak observations, then invokes three explicit unit-test collections and verifies all obsolete observations cleared. No force-GC is used in production or FPS/memory acceptance.

opt2_synthetic_pair.scope: Native Windows x86_64 Rust debug build, production-policy opt2 Luau interpreter, sampling disabled but VM allocation/incremental-GC diagnostic hooks enabled. This is a synthetic changing View, not a Web FPS or actual inventory result.
opt2_synthetic_pair.canonical_equality: Initial state and all 120 warmup snapshots are byte-equal; all warmup digests match. All 10 measured snapshots remain byte-equal.
opt2_synthetic_pair.comparison: Exact historical 0.5 package source versus corrected immutable 0.6 source, same authored View and injected 0.6 metadata in both VMs. The historical source fixture itself is unchanged.
opt2_synthetic_pair.allocation_method: Luau onallocate sum(max(new_size-old_size,0)) on successful requests; excludes frees, allocator overhead and Rust/JavaScript allocations
opt2_synthetic_pair.gc_method: Paired Luau incremental-step interrupts, including automatic assists and instrumentation overhead; steps are not whole collector cycles
opt2_synthetic_pair.max_step_disposition: The corrected immutable run has a larger maximum observed GC step despite lower total measured incremental time and fewer steps. This evidence does not establish a general pause improvement.

baseline_diagnostic_identity.scope: Matching 0.5 pre-change diagnostic artifacts were preserved before 0.6 tracked edits. Game inventory phase/stack attribution belongs to the owner-run evidence and is not invented or replaced by this synthetic pair.

independent_review.scope: Read-only source, exact intrinsic list, lifecycle/ownership, bounds and regression review. Reviewers' read-only work is separate from the author's executed commands.
independent_review.finding: P2 writable function-environment authority and equality-based managed-node spoofing
independent_review.disposition: Corrected through lexical capture of trusted intrinsics and raw identity; actual before-failure/after-success and adversarial regression executed

superseded_evidence.disposition: Historical cache-only results; not the final fixed-source pass count or allocation result. Superseded by the 33-test and corrected opt2 records above.

limitations: No official Web seven-scenario pass, inventory 60 FPS, OS presentation cadence, GPU or whole-player acceptance is claimed here
Short synthetic allocation/GC diagnostics are instrumented and cannot establish leak-free or GC-free behavior
The weak-reclamation unit proves the private grant map does not strongly retain the tested obsolete graphs; it is not a whole-engine memory leak proof
Full Luau GC time, JavaScript GC and Rust allocator traffic are unavailable in this pair and remain null or explicitly outside its scope
Breaking 0.6 constructor ownership requires matching canonical types/package/player/CLI and actual Game adoption validation before shipment
